verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              प्रवेशने तु पार्थानां जनानां पुरवासिनाम् । दिदृक्षूणां सहस्राणि समाजग्मुः सहस्रशः ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said 'All immobile and mobile beings, divided into four classes, have been described to be of unmanifest birth and unmanifest death. Existing only in the unmanifest Soul, the Mind is said to possess the attributes of the unmanifest.

verses.sanskrit: स राजमार्गः शुशुभे समलङ्कृतचत्वरः । यथा चन्द्रोदये राजन्वर्धमानो महोदधिः ॥२॥
verses.english: As a vast tree lies within a small unblown Ashvatha flower and is seen only when it comes out, so birth takes place from what is unmanifest.

verses.sanskrit: गृहाणि राजमार्गेषु रत्नवन्ति महान्ति च । प्राकम्पन्तीव भारेण स्त्रीणां पूर्णानि भारत ॥३॥
verses.english: A piece of iron, which is inanimate runs towards a piece of loadstone. Likewise, inclinations and propensities due to natural instincts, and all else, run towards the Soul in a 11cw lifc.

verses.sanskrit: ताः शनैरिव सव्रीडं प्रशशंसुर्युधिष्ठिरम् । भीमसेनार्जुनौ चैव माद्रीपुत्रौ च पाण्डवौ ॥४॥
verses.english: Indeed, as those propensities bom of Darkness and Ignorance, and inactive in their nature, are united with the Soul when re-born, similarly, those other inclinations and aspirations of the Soul that have their look directed towards Brahma become united with it, coming to it directly from Brahima itself.

verses.sanskrit: धन्या त्वमसि पाञ्चालि या त्वं पुरुषसत्तमान् । उपतिष्ठसि कल्याणि महर्षीनिव गौतमी ॥५॥
verses.english: Neither earth, nor sky, nor heaven, nor things, nor the vital airs, nor virtue and vice, nor anything else, existed before, except the Intelligence-Soul. Nor have they any necessary connection with even the Intelligence-Soul corrupted by Darkness.

verses.sanskrit: तव कर्माण्यमोघानि व्रतचर्या च भाविनि । इति कृष्णां महाराज प्रशशंसुस्तदा स्त्रियः ॥६॥
verses.english: The Soul is eternal. It is indestructible. It is in every creature. It is the cause of the Mind. It is without qualities. This universe before us is due to Darkness or Ignorance. The Soul's apprehensions of form, etc., are due to past desires.

verses.sanskrit: प्रशंसावचनैस्तासां मिथःशब्दैश्च भारत । प्रीतिजैश्च तदा शब्दैः पुरमासीत्समाकुलम् ॥७॥
verses.english: The Soul, when it becomes endued with desires, engages in acts. On account of that condition, this vast wheel of existence revolves with beginning and without end.

verses.sanskrit: तमतीत्य यथायुक्तं राजमार्गं युधिष्ठिरः । अलङ्कृतं शोभमानमुपायाद्राजवेश्म ह ॥८॥
verses.english: The Understanding, is the nave of that wheel. The body with the senses, forms its spokes. The perceptions and acts are its circumference. Urged by on the quality of Darkness, the Soul presides over it.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रकृतयः सर्वाः पौरा जानपदास्तदा । ऊचुः कर्णसुखा वाचः समुपेत्य ततस्ततः ॥९॥
verses.english: Like oilmen pressing oilseeds pressing oilseeds in their machine, the consequences born of Darkness, assailing the universe which is moistened by Darkness, press or grind it in that wheel.

verses.sanskrit: दिष्ट्या जयसि राजेन्द्र शत्रूञ्छत्रुनिषूदन । दिष्ट्या राज्यं पुनः प्राप्तं धर्मेण च बलेन च ॥१०॥
verses.english: In that succession of births, the individual Soul, seized by the idea of Ego in consequence of desire, performs acts. In the union of cause and effect, those acts again become fresh causes.

verses.sanskrit: भवनस्त्वं महाराज राजेह शरदां शतम् । प्रजाः पालय धर्मेण यथेन्द्रस्त्रिदिवं तथा ॥११॥
verses.english: Effects do not enter into causes. Nor do causes enter into effects. Time is the instrumental in the production of effects.

verses.sanskrit: एवं राजकुलद्वारि मङ्गलैरभिपूजितः । आशीर्वादान् द्विजैरुक्तान्प्रतिगृह्य समन्ततः ॥१२॥
verses.english: The primordial essences, and their changes endued with causes, exist unitedly, on account of their being always presided over by the Soul.

verses.sanskrit: प्रविश्य भवनं राजा देवराजगृहोपमम् । श्रद्धाविजयसंयुक्तं रथात्पश्चादवातरत् ॥१३॥
प्रविश्याभ्यन्तरं श्रीमान्दैवतान्यभिगम्य च । पूजयामास रत्नैश्च गन्धमाल्यैश्च सर्वशः ॥१४॥
निश्चक्राम ततः श्रीमान्पुनरेव महायशाः । ददर्श ब्राह्मणांश्चैव सोऽभिरूपानवस्थितान् ॥१५॥
स संवृतस्तदा विप्रैराशीर्वादविवक्षुभिः । शुशुभे विमलश्चन्द्रस्तारागणवृतो यथा ॥१६॥
तांस्तु वै पूजयामास कौन्तेयो विधिवद्द्विजान् । धौम्यं गुरुं पुरस्कृत्य ज्येष्ठं पितरमेव च ॥१७॥
सुमनोमोदकै रत्नैर्हिरण्येन च भूरिणा । गोभिर्वस्त्रैश्च राजेन्द्र विविधैश्च किमिच्छकैः ॥१८॥
ततः पुण्याहघोषोऽभूद्दिवं स्तब्ध्वेव भारत । सुहृदां प्रीतिजननः पुण्यः श्रुतिसुखावहः ॥१९॥
हंसवद्विदुषां राजा द्विजानां तत्र भारतीम् । शुश्रुवे वेदविदुषां पुष्कलार्थपदाक्षराम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: The king heard that sound uttered by those learned Brahmanas loud and clear like the sound of swans. He listened also to the melodious and significant speeches, of those persons well read in the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुन्दुभिनिर्घोषः शङ्खानां च मनोरमः । जयं प्रवदतां तत्र स्वनः प्रादुरभून्नृप ॥२१॥
verses.english: Then arose, O king, the peal of drums and the pleasant blare of conchs, indicative of triumph.

verses.sanskrit: निःशब्दे च स्थिते तत्र ततो विप्रजने पुनः । राजानं ब्राह्मणच्छद्या चार्वाको राक्षसोऽब्रवीत् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Some time after, when the Brahmanas had become silent, a Rakshasa of the name of Charvaka, who had disguised himself as a Brahmana, addressed the king.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र दुर्योधनसखा भिक्षुरूपेण संवृतः । साक्षः शिखी त्रिदण्डी च धृष्टो विगतसाध्वसः ॥२३॥
verses.english: He was a friend of Duryodhana and stood there under the disguise of a religious mendicant. With a rosary, with a tuft of hair on his head, and with a staff in his hand, he stood proudly and fearlessly in the midst of all those Brahmanas that had come there in thousands for uttering for blessings, (upon the king) O king, and all of whom had practised penances and vows.

verses.sanskrit: वृतः सर्वैस्तथा विप्रैराशीर्वादविवक्षुभिः । परं सहस्रै राजेन्द्र तपोनियमसंवृतैः ॥२४॥
स दुष्टः पापमाशंसुः पाण्डवानां महात्मनाम् । अनामन्त्र्यैव तान् विप्नांस्तमुवाच महीपतिम् ॥२५॥
verses.english: That wicked Rakshasa, desirous of doing evil to the high-souled Pandavas, and without having consulted those Brahmanas, said these words to the king.

verses.sanskrit: चार्वाक उवाच । इमे प्राहुर्द्विजाः सर्वे समारोप्य वचो मयि । धिग् भवन्तं कुनृपतिं ज्ञातिघातिनमस्तु वै ॥२६॥
verses.english: Charvaka said Making me their spokesman all these Brahmanas, are saying,-Fie on you. You are a wicked king. You are a destroyer of kinsmen.

verses.sanskrit: किं तेन स्याद्धि कौन्तेय कृत्वेमं ज्ञातिसंक्षयम् । घातयित्वा गुरूंश्चैव मृतं श्रेयो न जीवितम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: What will you gain, O son of Kunti, by having thus exterminated your race? Having killed also your elders and preceptor, it is proper for you to cast away your life.

verses.sanskrit: इति ते वै द्विजाः श्रुत्वा तस्य दुष्टस्य रक्षसः । विव्यथुश्चुक्रुशुश्चैव तस्य वाक्यप्रधर्षिताः ॥२८॥
verses.english: 'Hearing these words of that wicked Rakshasa, the Brahmanas there were greatly moved. Cut to the quick by that speech, they set up a loud uproar.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे स च राजा युधिष्ठिर । व्रीडिताः परमोद्विग्नास्तूष्णीमासन् विशाम्पते ॥२९॥
verses.english: And all those Brahmanas, with king Yudhishthira, O king, became silent from anxiety and shame.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              प्रसीदन्तु भवन्तो मे प्रणतस्याभियाचतः । प्रत्यासन्नव्यसनिनं न मां धिक्कर्तुमर्हथ ॥३०॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said I bow down to you and solicit you humbly, to be pleased with me. You should not cry fie on me. I shall soon cast off my life. not

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततो राजन् ब्राह्मणास्ते सर्व एव विशाम्पते । ऊचुर्नैतद्वचोऽस्माकं श्रीरस्तु तव पार्थिव ॥३१॥
verses.bhavadeepa: प्रत्यासन्नाः समीपस्थाः व्यसनिनश्चिरदुःखिनो भ्रात्रादयो यस्य तं भ्रात्रादिदुःखपरिहारार्थं ममेदं राज्यकरणं न तु स्वसुखार्थमित्यर्थः ॥३०॥

verses.sanskrit: जज्ञुश्चैव महात्मानस्ततस्तं ज्ञानचक्षुषा । ब्राह्मणा वेदविद्वांसस्तपोभिर्विमलीकृताः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Those great persons, well read in the Vedas, with understandings rendered clear by penances, then learnt the disguise of the speaker by means of their spiritual sight.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणा ऊचुः । एष दुर्योधनसखा चार्वाको नाम राक्षसः । परिव्राजकरूपेण हितं तस्य चिकीर्षति ॥३३॥
verses.english: This is the Rakshasa Charvaka, the friend of Duryodhana. Having put on the guise of a religious mendicant, he seeks the well-being of his friend Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: न वयं ब्रूम धर्मात्मन् व्येतु ते भयमीदृशम् । उपतिष्ठतु कल्याणं भवन्तं भ्रातृभिः सह ॥३४॥
verses.english: We have not, O you righteous soul, said anything of the kind. Drive away your anxiety. May prosperity be with you and your brothers.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              ततस्ते ब्राह्मणाः सर्वे हुंकारैः क्रोधमूर्छिताः । निर्भर्त्सयन्तः शुचयो निजघ्नुः पापराक्षसम् ॥३५॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Those Brahmanas then, beside themselves with anger, uttered the sound hum. Freed off of all sins, they censured the sinful Rakshasa and killed him there.

verses.sanskrit: स पपात विनिर्दग्धस्तेजसा ब्रह्मवादिनाम् । महेन्द्राशनिनिर्दग्धः पादपोऽङ्कुरवानिव ॥३६॥
verses.english: Consumed by by the power of those Brahmavadins, Charvaka fell down dead, like a tree with all its blasted spouts by the thunder of Indra.

verses.sanskrit: पूजिताश्च ययुर्विप्रा राजानमभिनन्द्य तम् । राजा च हर्षमापेदे पाण्डवः ससुहृज्जनः ॥३७॥
verses.english: Duly adored the Brahmanas went away, having pleased the king with their blessing. The royal son of Pandu also, with all his friends, became highly happy.
